title: Spirits, liqueurs and bitters
lead: What each spirit is made from, and the bottles that sweeten, flavor and finish a drink.

sections.name: How spirits are made

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Every spirit starts as something fermented.

know: Distilling concentrates the alcohol made by fermentation.
The Base decides the spirit: grain, agave, sugarcane or fruit.
Proof in the US is twice the alcohol by volume.
Oak adds color and flavor; most unaged spirits are clear.

sections.name: Whiskey

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Whiskey is grain, distilled and aged in oak.

know: Bourbon is American whiskey, at least 51% corn.
New Oak barrels, charred inside, are a must for bourbon.
Rye whiskey is at least 51% rye.
Scotch is made in Scotland and aged at least three years.
Irish whiskey is made in Ireland.

sections.name: Tequila, mezcal, gin and vodka

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Agave, juniper and a clean slate.

know: Tequila is made from blue Weber agave in Mexico.
Reposado rests at least 2 months in oak; añejo at least a year.
Mezcal is agave too, often roasted in pits, so it’s smoky.
Vodka is meant to be clean and neutral.

sections.name: Liqueurs, vermouth and bitters

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Small pours that shape the drink.

know: Liqueur is a spirit with sugar and flavor added.
Orange liqueurs: triple sec, Cointreau, Grand Marnier.
Vermouth is flavored, fortified wine. Keep it cold once open.
Bitters go in by the dash: Angostura, Peychaud’s, orange.

read.bigIdea: Every spirit starts as something fermented.
read.where: Yeast turns sugar into alcohol. **Distilling** heats it and collects the alcohol, making it stronger. The start decides the spirit: **grain** for whiskey, **agave** for tequila and mezcal, **sugarcane** for rum, **grapes or other fruit** for brandy. In the US, **proof** is twice the ABV: 40% ABV is 80 proof.

read.bigIdea: Whiskey is grain, distilled and aged in oak.
read.where: **Bourbon** is made in the US from at least **51% corn** and aged in **new, charred oak** containers. **Rye** whiskey is at least **51% rye**, so it tastes spicier. **Scotch** is made in Scotland and aged at least **three years**. **Irish** whiskey is made in Ireland.
read.mixup: **Bourbon** has to be made in the US, but not only in Kentucky.
read.sayIt: Rye is a little spicier; bourbon is a little sweeter.

read.bigIdea: Agave, juniper and a clean slate.
read.where: **Tequila** is made in Mexico from **blue Weber agave**. **Blanco** is unaged or barely rested, **reposado** rests in oak at least two months, **añejo** at least a year. **Mezcal** is agave too; roasting it in pits makes it **smoky**. **Gin** tastes of **juniper**. **Vodka** is meant to be clean and neutral.
read.mixup: **Reposado** rests at least two months. **Añejo** rests at least a year.

read.bigIdea: Small pours that shape the drink.
read.where: A **liqueur** is a spirit with sugar and flavor added. **Orange liqueurs** (triple sec, Cointreau, Grand Marnier) sweeten many sours. **Vermouth** is wine that’s flavored and fortified; once open it fades like wine, so it lives in the **fridge**. **Bitters** are strong flavorings used a **dash** at a time: Angostura, Peychaud’s, orange.
